workTitle: Symphony No. 41 in C major, K. 551

clues.label: A biographical detail
clues.text: The composer was exhibited across Europe as a child prodigy by his father, playing for aristocratic courts before the age of ten.

clues.label: A historical event connected to the composer
clues.text: In 1781 the composer broke with his employer, an archbishop, and set up in the imperial capital as a freelance musician - an unusual and financially risky step for the period.

clues.label: A musical characteristic
clues.text: The finale handles five distinct themes in invertible counterpoint, stacking them on top of one another in the closing bars.

clues.label: Places the composer lived and worked
clues.text: Born in a prince-archbishop's town on the Salzach, the composer spent his last decade in the imperial capital and died there in 1791, aged thirty-five. This work belongs to that final decade.

explanation.summary: A Salzburg prodigy who went freelance in Vienna, and a finale that stacks five themes at once: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, Vienna, 1788.

points.text: The scale and duration of the childhood tours, managed by his father Leopold, are unique to Mozart.
The 1781 break with Archbishop Colloredo marks the move from Salzburg to Vienna.
A finale combining five themes in invertible counterpoint is the "Jupiter" Symphony, K. 551.
The town on the Salzach is Salzburg — the birthplace, but not the answer here. The last three symphonies were written in Vienna in the summer of 1788.
